goal: Blocked steps are the brief's work. The brief document gathers them as their own section, the brief role says what the session does with each, and the ones a session can settle by reading are settled at the brief instead of waiting for a programme's planning session to come round to them.

Today nothing gathers them. Measured on 2026-09-05 from `~/mc/runner/plans.json` (memoro at `721f9a07`), **48 steps on `origin/main` are `blocked`** across both repositories — 28 on a `project` blocker and 20 on a `decision`. `renderBrief` (`src/mc/brief-collect.js:667`) has twelve sections and not one of them is about a blocked step; the only trace is inside *Plan status*, where each plan gets one row and the blocker arrives clipped to 110 characters inside the `next` cell. `canon/roles/brief.md` names four kinds of work — held before merge, ready-but-the-runner-will-not-start-it, production, and the two tidying lists — and a blocked step is in none of them.

Martin, 2026-09-05: *"Din uppgift som roll brief är att hjälpa mig att ta hand om blocked steps. Allting som är enkelt som inte kräver djupare analys i en programmets plan-session ska du fixa åt mig."*
contract: **Three kinds, told apart before anything else.** A `project` blocker is ordinary sequencing and is not a question: 28 of the 48 are that, and 26 of those are the sql-readiness families waiting on each other in a deliberate order. A `decision` blocker named `plan-review` is a programme's planning session's — 12 of the 20 decision blockers carry that one name, across eight programmes, and none of them has ever been a question put to Martin. What is left is 8 named decisions, and those are the brief's to sort into what it can settle and what only Martin can answer.

**Simple means the estate already holds the answer.** A blocker whose decision was answered somewhere else, one naming a project that has since landed, one whose name is not a name — those a brief session settles by reading, and says what it read. Anything that needs the plan's own reasoning re-opened goes to that programme's planning session, and anything that needs Martin's judgement is put to him as one proposal with one recommendation, which is what the role already says about held pull requests.

**The brief still writes no plan's steps out of turn.** A step session's authority over `steps[index]` and the runner's before/after comparison (`docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what*) do not change. What changes is that a brief session may unblock a step it has settled, and step 2 is where that route is decided rather than assumed — the honest candidates are a pull request per fix, one pull request per brief carrying all of them, or a verb.

**No blocker is unblocked without its reason written down.** The line that says what was read and why the block is gone goes in the step's `comments`, in the same edit, so the next reader of the plan sees the answer and not just the state change.
out_of_scope: The 26 sql-readiness `project` blockers and the order the families close in. That order is `sql-readiness`'s own design and this project reads it, never moves it.

Answering any of the 8 named decisions. `mc-dev-1`, `plan-read-from-main-1`, `lanes-pair`, `msr-core-email-verified`, `mail-window-overlay-integrity-phone-confirmation`, `i18n-legacy-pages`, `i18n-text-leaf-fallback` and the sql promotion ruling are each Martin's or a programme's, and each is put to him one at a time at a brief. This project builds the surface that puts them there; it does not settle them.

Validating `blocked_by.name` against `NAME_RE`. `plan-schema.js:38` defines it and `validateBlocker` (`:140`) checks only that the name is non-empty text, which is how `sql-goal1-certification` step 4 came to carry a 79-character sentence as a blocker name. Reporting that as its own fact is step 1's; making the schema refuse it would make every plan carrying one unrunnable the moment it lands, and that is a separate decision with its own proposal behind it.

`mc`'s page. The page's PROGRAMMES block already says `blocked 33 · ready 11` and names each blocker in its own row; whether it should also group them is not what was asked for and not needed for the brief to work.
The other six role files. `canon/roles/plan.md` is touched only to the extent that it has to know it is the receiving end of a `plan-review` hand-off.

success_criteria.criterion: The brief document has a *Blocked* section that tells the three kinds apart and does not make a reader open a plan to see what a step waits on.
success_criteria.check: Run `mc brief --collect` against the real estate and read the section: every blocked step appears with its programme, project, step number, blocker kind and the blocker's full name, grouped so that project blockers, `plan-review` blockers and named decisions are three separate lists with a count each. Asserted in `tests/mc/brief-collect.test.js` against a fixture holding one of each.

success_criteria.criterion: A blocker naming a project that is not on main, and a blocker whose name is not a name, are each reported as themselves rather than folded into the others.
success_criteria.check: The fixture carries a blocker naming a project that has landed and one carrying a sentence; the rendered section names both cases in their own words. Measured against the real estate at the same time and the count written into the pull request — it was 0 and 1 respectively on 2026-09-05.

success_criteria.criterion: `canon/roles/brief.md` tells a brief session that blocked steps are its work, which of the three kinds it settles itself, and what it does with the other two.
success_criteria.check: Read the file. A session that had only ever read the role, and not this plan, would take the same three routes; and the route by which a brief's own unblocking reaches `main` is named in it, not left to be worked out.

success_criteria.criterion: The route works once, end to end, on a real blocked step.
success_criteria.check: One blocked step in the estate is unblocked by a brief session through the route step 2 decided, with the reason in the step's `comments`, and the next `mc run` round hands that step out. Named in the close-out with what it was and what was read to settle it.

steps.title: The brief gathers blocked steps, and tells the three kinds apart
steps.done_when: `renderBrief` writes a *Blocked* section, `mc brief --collect` shows it against the real estate, and the counts in the pull request body match a hand count of `~/mc/runner/plans.json`.
instruction: Start by reading what is already there rather than adding beside it. `listPlans` (`brief-collect.js:224`) already parses every `PLAN.json` on `origin/main` for both repositories and `planFields` (`:169`) already reduces each to the fields the *Plan status* table shows. The blocked steps are in that same parsed plan and are being thrown away — nothing new needs fetching, and this section costs no extra git call.

Group by what the reader will do next, not by repository. Three lists: **project blockers** (28 on 2026-09-05, of which 26 are sql-readiness families in a deliberate order) which are sequencing and want a count and nothing more; **`plan-review`** (12, across eight programmes) which is a hand-off to that programme's planning session and wants the programme named so the hand-off can be made; and **named decisions** (8) which is the list a brief session actually works through, and wants the blocker's full name uncut, the step's title, and how long the step has stood blocked if that is cheaply knowable.

Two facts inside the third list are worth their own line, because both are invisible today and both are cheap. A project blocker naming a project that is not on `origin/main` is either delivered or abandoned and a person has to say which — `staleBlockers` (`src/mc/stale-blockers.js`) already computes exactly this for the page and should be reused rather than rewritten. And a blocker name that does not match `NAME_RE` (`plan-schema.js:38`) is neither a live blocker nor a finished one but a plan that cannot be checked: `sql-goal1-certification` step 4 carries `"promotion of sql_migration_ready on the certified commit — Martin's explicit ruling, never inferred"` as a name. Report that as its own case. Do not add the validation to the schema — that is out of scope and has a proposal of its own.

Where the section goes matters for how the brief reads top to bottom. *Held before merge* and *Ready, and the runner cannot start it* are the two sections that already mean "a project is standing still and it is yours"; blocked steps are the third and largest of that family, and belong beside them rather than after *Queue*.
The counts in the pull request body should be measured, not copied from this plan: it was 48/28/20 with 12 `plan-review` on 2026-09-05 and the estate moves daily.
comments: Measured against `~/mc/runner/plans.json` (memoro `38e5b57`, memoro-cli `d443915`, read 2026-09-05T20:33Z) and confirmed by a real `mc brief --collect` the same evening: **45 blocked steps**, not the plan's 48 — 28 project, 12 `plan-review` across six programmes (not eight), 5 named decisions. The five are `i18n-legacy-pages`, `i18n-text-leaf-fallback`, `msr-core-email-verified`, `lanes-pair` and the sql promotion ruling; `mc-dev-1`, `plan-read-from-main-1` and the two mail/phone decisions the plan's out_of_scope names are no longer blocking anything on main. The two special cases stand at 0 stale and 1 not-a-name, as the plan predicted — and the sql promotion ruling's blocker name is 99 characters, not 79.

The section is `blockedSteps` (brief-collect.js) plus `blockedLines`, and it costs no git call: it reads the same parsed plans `listPlans` already fetched for *Plan status*, and reuses `staleBlockers` for the not-on-main case rather than recomputing it. Grouping is by what the reader does, not by `blocked_by.kind`: `plan-review` is a `decision` by kind and a hand-off by meaning, so `row.group` is one of `project` / `plan-review` / `decision` while `row.kind` stays the schema's word. Step 2 has the fields it needs to build a route on — repo, programme, project, step number, title, kind, full blocker name, `stale`, `unnamed`.
`NAME_RE` in `plan-schema.js` was defined and used by nothing; it is now exported and read by `blockedSteps`, which is the only reader. No validation was added — that is out of scope and stays so.

The verification run of `mc brief --collect` wrote `~/mc/brief/2026-09-05T20-43-27Z.md` and I deleted it again afterwards, so the estate's "since last brief" window still stands at 2026-09-04T16:10Z and the next real brief does not lose a day of merged pull requests.

steps.title: The role says blocked steps are the brief's, and by what route
steps.done_when: `canon/roles/brief.md` carries the three routes and the mechanism by which a brief session's unblocking reaches `main`; `canon/roles/plan.md` knows it receives `plan-review` hand-offs.
instruction: This step writes the paragraph the whole project is for, so write it in the file's own voice — short, concrete, and telling the session what to do rather than what the mechanism is. The existing sections about *Held before merge* and the two tidying lists are the model: each names what the thing is, what the session may decide, and what it must not touch.

The three routes, in the order a session meets them. A **project blocker** is sequencing and needs nothing said unless the project it names is not on `origin/main`, in which case somebody has to say whether it was delivered or abandoned, and that is a sentence in the brief and not a fix. **`plan-review`** is not a question for Martin and never was: it is a step waiting for its programme's planning session, and what a brief session owes it is to say so and name the programme, so `mc plan <programme>` is the next thing rather than another brief passing it over. A **named decision** is the one to work: read the plan and the code behind it, and if the answer is already in the estate — the decision answered under another name, the blocking project landed, the name not a name — settle it and write what was read into the step's `comments`. Only what a reading cannot settle is put to Martin, one proposal, one recommendation, the way a held pull request already is.

Then the part that does not exist yet and has to be decided here rather than left implied: **how a brief session's edit reaches `main`.** The brief has no workarea and makes none, and `docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what* gives step edits to the step session and plans to the planning session, so an unblocking by the brief is a fourth writer and needs a route said out loud. The honest candidates, with what each costs: a pull request per unblocked step from a scratch worktree, which is one pull request per fix and a lot of them; one pull request per brief carrying every unblocking that brief made, which reads as one decision and is easier for Martin to review as a whole; or a verb (`mc unblock <repo> <project> <step>`) that does the edit, the commit and the pull request, which is the only one that leaves nothing to remember but is also the only one that is code. Take one, say why in the pull request, and write the chosen one into the role — a route that is not in the role will not be taken.

`canon/roles/plan.md` gets one sentence, no more: a step blocked on `plan-review` is this session's to resolve, and the brief will have named it. Keep it to that — the plan role was cut to 219 lines across all seven roles by `role-instructions` and this is not the place to grow it back.
comments: The route chosen, and written into the role: **one pull request per repository per brief**, not one per unblocked step and not a verb. A plan is a file under `docs/`, so `mc merge <repo> <pr> --docs` (docs-merge.js) lands it with no suite at all and refuses anything outside `docs/` by GitHub's own file list — the brief already lands held pull requests by hand, so this needs no new authority and no new code, which is what killed `mc unblock`: step 3 has to walk the route, and a route that has to be built first cannot be walked in the step that walks it. The geography is load-bearing twice over and both halves were read rather than assumed. The worktree goes at `~/mc/brief/unblock/<repo>`, one level below `~/mc/brief/`, because `mc run`'s `workareas()` (run.js:924) and `areasWithCheckout()` list a top-level directory only when `<area>/<repo>` is a checkout — the same reason `~/mc/plan/` and `~/mc/gate/` are invisible. And the branch is `brief/unblock-<date>` because `projectForBranch` (project-prs.js:34) claims `<project>` and `<project>-…` for a project: a branch of either shape would read as that project's work in flight and end its round.

**`canon/roles/plan.md` was not edited, and the sentence went into `planLaunch`'s prompt (`src/mc/commands/plan.js`) instead — read this before assuming the file was missed.** That role file is frontmatter with no body by decision, and the decision is asserted: `tests/mc/commands/plan.test.js:41` checks `role.overlay === null`, its comment carrying the reason, and `planLaunch` inlines `canon/roles/_common.md` into the prompt *because* the role has no overlay — so giving plan.md a body would both break that assertion and hand a planning session the shared text twice, once through `instructionsFor` and once inside the prompt. The prompt is what a planning session is told (Martin, 2026-08-31), so that is where the hand-off now is, asserted by a new test beside the guard that keeps the prompt from growing back. The intent of `done_when` is met — a planning session is told a `plan-review` park is its own — but the file it names is not the file that changed.

For step 3: the estate's five named decisions are all genuine questions (measured in step 1), and the two special cases stood at 0 stale and 1 not-a-name, so the settle-by-reading case the route exists for may not be present on the day. The one that is closest is the `sql-goal1-certification` step 4 blocker whose name is a 99-character sentence — a blocker nothing can check, and the step it stops is a real one. If nothing is settleable, the step's instruction says to say so and name what would have to be true rather than manufacture one.

steps.title: Close out
steps.done_when: The route has been walked once on a real blocked step, `docs/technical/` says what the brief now does with blocked steps, and `docs/project/project_log.md` has the row.
instruction: Walk the route once rather than describing it. Pick one blocked step the estate already answers — the 12 `plan-review` ones are not it, and neither are the 8 named decisions unless one of them has been answered since — unblock it by the route step 2 chose, with the reason in `comments`, and watch the next `mc run` round hand it out. If nothing in the estate is settleable on the day, say that in the pull request and name what would have to be true; do not manufacture one.
The documentation half belongs with the brief, not with the runner: `docs/technical/` has the file that describes what a brief session is and does, and this is a change to that, not to `mc-run.md`.
comments: **The route was not walked on a real blocked step, because on 2026-09-05 the estate had none to walk it on.** Every blocked step was read, not sampled: all 5 named decisions are genuine questions of Martin's — `msr-core-email-verified` is his explicit gate that the email side is verified in the running app and `msr-core/README.md` names `mail-window-round-5` as that side's open work; `i18n-legacy-pages` and `i18n-text-leaf-fallback` are two rulings the plan's own steps say to ask for with the file list in hand; `lanes-pair` is `total-lane-cap` step 4's reserved question, whose own instruction forbids a session raising `per_repo` on its judgement; and the sql promotion is Martin's alone by `readiness-contract.md`. All 28 project blockers name a project that still has unfinished steps (checked one by one against the blocking plan's own step statuses, not only through `staleBlockers`, which is 0). The 12 `plan-review` parks are hand-offs by definition. The one unnamed blocker is the sql promotion — a live ruling with a bad name, not a dead block, so setting it `ready` would have been the manufacture the instruction forbids. What would have to be true: one blocked step whose answer the estate already holds — a decision answered under another name, a blocking project that has landed, or a name that is not a name on a block that is actually gone. Criterion 4 is left `met: false` for the next brief session to meet.

What could be verified by running rather than by reading was, so the role does not send a brief session down an untested route. With a real worktree at `~/mc/brief/unblock/memoro-cli` on branch `brief/unblock-2026-09-05` cut from `origin/main`: `areasWithCheckout` (status-collect.js) listed 80 areas and neither `brief` nor `unblock` was among them — both it and the runner's `workareas()` list a top-level directory only when `<area>/<repo>/.git` exists, and the worktree is a level below that; and `projectForBranch('brief/unblock-2026-09-05')` returned `null` against the 46 project names on main, where the control `brief-blocked-steps-4` returned `brief-blocked-steps`. The worktree and the branch were removed afterwards. What remains unrun is only the plan edit itself and the `mc merge --docs` landing, which is shipped machinery this project reuses rather than adds.

The documentation half is `docs/technical/mc-brief.md`: the section count went twelve to thirteen, *Blocked* has its own row in *What it reads* and its own passage beside *Ready, and the runner cannot start it*, and *How an answer travels* gained § *When the brief itself is the writer* — the route, the two geography facts with the numbers above, and why `mc unblock` was not built. `docs/technical/mc-run.md` was deliberately not touched: the runner does not know the brief exists and nothing about a round changed.

For whoever meets criterion 4: `mc brief --collect` was not run in this session, so the estate's "since last brief" window still stands at 2026-09-04T16:10Z. The measurement above came from `listPlans` + `blockedSteps` against both real `origin/main`s directly, which is the same reading the section renders from and writes no brief file.
